services.title: DWI
services.summary: First, second and third DWI charges.
services.text: In Texas, DWI charges can carry serious consequences, including fines, license suspension, probation, mandatory alcohol education programs and even jail time.
services.lead: If you are arrested for DWI in Montgomery or Harris County, you have only 15 days to act to protect your driving privileges. You face two cases: the criminal case brought by the State of Texas, and the license suspension from the Texas Department of Public Safety.
services.imageAlt: Justin Fowles's hands on a leather folio beside his nameplate

covers.title: First-time DWI
covers.text: Typically a Class B misdemeanor, with fines up to $2,000, 3 days to 6 months in county jail and a 3-month to 2-year license suspension.

covers.title: Second DWI
covers.text: A Class A misdemeanor, with fines up to $4,000, 1 month to 1 year in county jail and a 6-month to 2-year license suspension.

covers.title: Third DWI
covers.text: Fines up to $10,000, 2 to 10 years in prison and a 6-month to 2-year license suspension.

covers.title: Test results
covers.text: Breath, blood and urine results can be shown unreliable because of calibration issues, human error, instrument problems or medical circumstances.

covers.title: License protection
covers.text: Refusing a breath or blood test suspends your license for six months, but contacting us quickly after an arrest may help you keep it.

covers.title: Expunged or sealed records
covers.text: We assess your DWI case to see whether you are eligible to have records expunged or sealed.

questions.q: What happens if I refuse a breathalyzer in Texas?
questions.a: If you refuse a breathalyzer test in Texas, you may face an automatic suspension of your driver's license for 180 days, and the refusal may be used against you in court.

questions.q: How long will a DWI stay on my record in Texas?
questions.a: A DWI conviction in Texas remains on your criminal record permanently unless you are eligible for expungement, which can be a complex process.

questions.q: How do you charge for a DWI case?
questions.a: Our pricing is a flat rate with no hidden fees, and we offer flexible payment plans.

questions.q: What could happen to me if convicted?
questions.a: Depending on the circumstances, a jury could find you guilty of a misdemeanor or a felony. Misdemeanors usually mean some time in jail or on probation, and under certain circumstances the prosecutor can upgrade the charge to a felony. Long-term consequences can include trouble finding work, losing custody of children and limits on firearm ownership.

faqs.q: When do I need a criminal attorney?
faqs.a: Legal protection is not just for after charges are filed. It starts when an investigation begins, before any official accusation.
Seek counsel from an experienced criminal defense attorney. Every word you say to investigators can be used against you later, so do not risk self-incrimination.

faqs.q: Can I get bail and be released?
faqs.a: You are generally entitled to bail after an arrest in Texas. Contact us, and our criminal defense lawyer can help you secure a bail bond for a prompt 24-hour jail release.
Missing a court appearance often leads to a bench warrant, which puts you at risk of arrest. We make sure your rights are protected and the correct procedures are followed.

faqs.q: Should I defend myself at trial?
faqs.a: The law may allow it, but we strongly discourage it. The court will hold you to the same standard as an experienced criminal defense lawyer.

faqs.q: Can a conviction be cleared from my record?
faqs.a: Depending on your case, we can help clean up your record through expunctions or nondisclosures.
